title: Cyrus and the Veil
premise: Gideon Dunmore, exiled to a valley where magic cannot follow, has spent ten years learning to be ordinary. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands and names him heir to an unfinished oath, Gideon is dragged beyond the Veil into a kingdom where the young king Aldric is slowly being consumed by the crown that rules him — a parasitic intelligence called the Regent that eats memories and rewrites loyalties. Hunted by the Regent's inquisitors and shadowed by Wren, a memory-thief who knew the dead courier, Gideon must gather three shattered keystones of the original binding before the coronation renewal rite makes the possession permanent. In the end Gideon chooses justice over vengeance: rather than destroy the king with the parasite, he takes the crown's burden onto his own storm-torn mind long enough for Wren to unbind it, sacrificing his memories of the valley — and discovering that belonging was never a place he lost, but people he finally chose.
about_author: Tamsin Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we cannot bear to remember. She writes from a drafty coastal cottage, accompanied by an opinionated cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Ten years after exile, he tends goats and buries his storm-calling under routine; a tremor in his hands betrays the magic still caged inside him. Emotional beat: numb resignation masking grief for the life magic cost him.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A bleeding man collapses at the river crossing, pursued by something unseen; his wounds smoke as if burned from within. Emotional beat: dread — the outside world has found the one place it shouldn't reach.

chapters.title: The Map and the Oath
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The dying courier, Sera Voss, presses a map into his hands, speaks his true name, and dies mid-sentence: 'Tell the king his father—' Emotional beat: unwilling inheritance; Gideon wants to burn the map and can't.

chapters.title: What Follows the Dying
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Grey-robed inquisitors arrive searching for the courier, sniffing out residual magic; Gideon lies badly and realizes the valley is no longer safe. Emotional beat: fear hardening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: Crossing the Veil
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He follows the map to the valley's edge and steps through; sensation floods back — wind, power, the storm answering his pulse for the first time in a decade. Emotional beat: terror and terrible homecoming at once.

chapters.title: The Thief on the Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A pickpocket lifts Gideon's pack, finds Sera's map, and recognizes her dead mentor's handwriting; she shadows the storm-caller instead of fleeing. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She saves Gideon from an inquisitor trap in a border town by trading a stolen memory to buy their escape. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Not Alone
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The young king wakes with hours missing and ink on hands he doesn't remember using; the crown whispers approval. Emotional beat: quiet horror dressed up as duty.

chapters.title: The Regent Explains
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The entity in the crown shows him 'memories' of his father's madness, justifying its guardianship; Aldric almost believes. Emotional beat: gaslit tenderness — captivity that feels like care.

chapters.title: Keystone One: The Bellfounder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Gideon and Wren's alternating POV. They trace the first keystone to a drowned bell-tower guarded by a ghost who demands a truth in payment. Emotional beat: the cost of honesty between strangers.

chapters.title: Storms Answer Him
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cornered by inquisitors, Gideon calls lightning for the first time since exile and is sickened by how good it feels. Emotional beat: the seduction of the thing that ruined him.

chapters.title: The Archive of Stolen Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leads them to the thieves' archive where stolen memories are bought and sold; she finds a vial labeled with Sera's name. Emotional beat: hope curdling — someone sold her mentor's last words.

chapters.title: Sera's Last Words
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Playing back the memory, they learn Sera discovered the Regent's origin: it was bound once before, by a king who chose to forget how. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into mission.

chapters.title: The Court of Whispered Edicts
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. At court, the Regent purges a loyal minister whose doubt it tastes; Aldric signs the order with his own hand. Emotional beat: complicity — the moment he stops being only a victim.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Inn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The party is betrayed by a friendly tinker; Wren is captured while Gideon escapes with the first keystone. Emotional beat: survivor's shame — he ran, again.

chapters.title: The Questioner's Cell
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An inquisitor extracts memories drop by drop; Wren feeds him false ones and guards the location of the second keystone. Emotional beat: defiance as identity — she is what she refuses to give up.

chapters.title: The Bargain with Brannoc
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. To find Wren, Gideon bargains with Brannoc, a smuggler-king who knew Sera and wants the map's route in return. Emotional beat: moral compromise — justice purchased with dirty coin.

chapters.title: Breaking the Questioner
chapters.summary: Gideon and Brannoc's POV. A raid frees Wren, but she has lost the memory of her own sister's face. Emotional beat: rescue that arrives too late for some things; rage kindled.

chapters.title: Keystone Two: The Weeping Quarry
chapters.summary: Gideon and Wren's POV. The second keystone lies in a quarry where stone remembers every hand that cut it; the stone tests Gideon's exile story and finds the lie in it. Emotional beat: confession — why he was really banished.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Valley
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He admits he wasn't exiled for a crime but fled after his storm killed his brother during a duel of pride. Emotional beat: unburdening; Wren stays anyway, which undoes him more than judgment would.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The Regent grows careless; Aldric glimpses a real memory beneath the planted ones — his father screaming warnings. Emotional beat: the first crack of agency.

chapters.title: Letters in the Wall
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric finds his father's hidden correspondence naming the binding ritual and the third keystone's keeper. Emotional beat: inherited courage — a dead king's faith reaching across years.

chapters.title: The Renewal Rite Announced
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Coronation renewal is set for the solstice; the Regent will make its hold permanent before the assembled realm. Emotional beat: clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Gideon and Wren's POV. The third keystone's keeper is a blind oracle who was once the Regent's first host, kept alive as a warning. Emotional beat: horror and pity — a preview of Aldric's future.

chapters.title: What the Oracle Sees
chapters.summary: Oracle's POV. She reads Gideon's storm and Wren's thefts and offers the keystone for a price: one of them must carry the crown's burden when it is torn free. Emotional beat: prophecy as sentence.

chapters.title: Neither Will Say Yes
chapters.summary: Gideon and Wren's POV. Each secretly plans to take the price themselves; each lies to the other about it. Emotional beat: love arriving disguised as argument.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Brannoc sells their route to the inquisitors for a pardon; the ambush at Hollowmere costs the smuggler his life defending them — a debt repaid too late. Emotional beat: betrayal and unexpected grace in the same breath.

chapters.title: Three Stones, One Binding
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The keystones fuse into a key that responds only to willing hands; the oracle teaches them the unbinding rite, which requires the host's consent. Emotional beat: the plan's fatal flaw — Aldric must choose.

chapters.title: The King's Secret Audience
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric, following his father's letters, slips his guards and meets Gideon and Wren in the undercroft. Emotional beat: three conspirators, one terrified and hopeful.

chapters.title: Consent Is the Lock
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Told the price of unbinding, Aldric insists he should pay it — he owes his kingdom a whole self, not a borrowed martyr. Emotional beat: nobility that frustrates everyone.

chapters.title: The Regent Hunts
chapters.summary: Regent's POV (unusual, cold). The crown senses its host slipping and unleashes the full inquisition; the city locks down before the solstice. Emotional beat: the antagonist's chilling logic — it genuinely believes it is saving the realm.

chapters.title: Riot of the Remembered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren releases stolen memories into the city square — thousands of citizens suddenly recall what the Regent erased. Emotional beat: uprising born of returned grief; chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: The Solstice Rite Begins
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Dragged to the altar by the Regent, Aldric stalls the renewal rite with a speech seeded with his father's forbidden words. Emotional beat: a boy out-talking a god, barely.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Cathedral
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon and Wren fight through inquisitors to the altar; Gideon embraces the storm fully, letting it tear the roof open above the rite. Emotional beat: the weapon he feared becomes the tool of rescue.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The rite tears the Regent loose — but it seizes Gideon instead of dissipating, and Wren must drive the key home while he holds it. Emotional beat: climax; trust as the final instrument.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Regent burns out of him, taking the valley, his brother's face, ten years of exile — everything soft. Emotional beat: hollow victory; he saved a kingdom and lost his past.

chapters.title: What Wren Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns a single stolen vial to Gideon: Sera's memory of him, so he knows he was loved even if he can't feel it. Emotional beat: tenderness as restitution.

chapters.title: A King Made Whole
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Freed, Aldric abolishes the crown's enchantments and begins reckoning with the court's complicity — justice without executions. Emotional beat: repair over revenge.

chapters.title: The Valley, Unmapped
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon visits the valley he can no longer remember and feels nothing but peace; the storm in him is quiet, chosen rather than caged. Emotional beat: acceptance — memory lost, self intact.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. On the palace steps at dawn, Gideon, Wren, and Aldric watch the first storm of the new reign roll in — invited this time. Emotional beat: resolution; home is the people who stayed.
